institution: IRCAM — Institut de Recherche et Coordination Acoustique/Musique
program: Cursus — Programme on Composition and Computer Music
qualification: NOT A DEGREE — a one-year non-diploma professional training programme (850 hours) in composition and computer music. IRCAM itself awards no master's. Only students ALREADY enrolled in the composition master's at CNSMD Lyon or HEAR Strasbourg may, after separate jury selection, have a Cursus year counted towards their master's at those schools.
accreditationStatus: Not an accredited degree. IRCAM is a research institute (association) attached to Centre Pompidou; it has no degree-awarding power of its own.
language: English ('Courses are taught in English')
durationEcts: 1 year, 12 Oct 2026 – 30 Sep 2027; 850 hours. No ECTS.
whatYouStudy: IRCAM software and practice: Max, OpenMusic, Modalys, ASAP, Partiel, Spat; sound synthesis, spatialisation, real-time interaction, score-following; mini-projects per unit then a final piece premiered at the opening of the IRCAM season in September.
entryRequirements: Composers under the age of 37 (born after 1 January 1987). Applicants are expected to be practising composers — selection is on artistic dossier.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — no formal degree requirement is stated (no music degree is demanded), but selection is on a composer's portfolio, so a candidate with no works has effectively no case. Page states only: 'open to composers under the age of 37'.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED from the public page — application runs through calls.ircam.fr; scores/recordings of existing works are required there. Exact number/length not confirmed.
auditionSpec: No live audition confirmed; selection is by dossier/jury. UNVERIFIED whether an interview stage exists.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 2,000 participation fee for the year (same for all nationalities)
otherFees: Accommodation 'to be borne by the participants'; Paris living costs; visa.
totalCostEstimate: EUR 2,000 fee + approx. EUR 14,000–18,000/yr Paris living = approx. EUR 16,000–20,000
scholarships: No scholarships or grants mentioned on the Cursus/Ulysses call page. UNVERIFIED whether Ulysses Network mobility support applies.
languageRequirement: English; no test stated
deadline: 3 December 2025 for the 2026-2027 edition — PRIOR CYCLE. The equivalent 2027-2028 deadline would be approx. early December 2026.
verdictForCandidate: NOT A MASTER'S. No student visa route as a degree student, no ECTS. Requires an existing composer portfolio. Record it to close the loop: IRCAM's Cursus is NOT the master's people assume it is.

institution: Sorbonne Université, with IRCAM and Télécom Paris
program: Master ATIAM — Acoustique, Traitement du signal et Informatique Appliqués à la Musique
qualification: Master's degree in Sciences and Technologies (M2 year only), awarded by Sorbonne Université — mention Informatique (SAR) or Sciences pour l'Ingénieur (acoustique)
accreditationStatus: State-accredited French master (diplôme national de master), Sorbonne Université
language: French (courses largely in French; UNVERIFIED whether any are in English)
durationEcts: M2 only: 30 ECTS taught (5 modules x 6 ECTS) + 5–6 month research internship = 60 ECTS for the year
whatYouStudy: Musical acoustics, sound signal processing, music informatics, MIR, synthesis, computer-aided composition. Research-track, scientific — NOT an artistic composition degree.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'a first year of Master's experience or hold a M1 French degree (or equivalent)'. Also 'an excellent understanding of at least two of the three main domains — acoustics, signal processing, or computer science — and show a strong interest in music.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — it is explicitly a scientific master; no music degree required. BUT a bachelor alone is NOT enough: 'Bachelor's holders cannot directly enter — a completed first year of Master's study is mandatory.' A 3-year Tunisian BSc would need an M1 first (or an engineering diploma).
portfolioSpec: No artistic portfolio. Academic dossier: transcripts, CV, motivation letter, description of scientific and musical background.
auditionSpec: NO live audition. Selection 'on a file basis' by the teaching team.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — Sorbonne Université applies national master fee (approx. EUR 250/yr) but France's 'frais différenciés' for non-EU can be EUR 3,879/yr unless exempted; Sorbonne has historically exempted. Must be confirmed.
otherFees: CVEC approx. EUR 105/yr; Paris living approx. EUR 1,200–1,500/month
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — approx. EUR 15,000–20,000/yr dominated by living costs
scholarshipName: Campus France / Eiffel Excellence Scholarship (nominated by the institution)
languageRequirement: French (candidate is fluent — an advantage here)
deadline: UNVERIFIED — see https://www.atiam.ircam.fr/candidatures/ ; typically spring (March–April) for September entry
verdictForCandidate: BLOCKED AT ENTRY for a 3-year BSc: ATIAM is M2-only and requires a completed M1. Also it is a science/research master, not an artist-maker degree. Would suit him after an M1 in France, not directly in 2027.

institution: Institute of Sonology, Royal Conservatoire The Hague (Koninklijk Conservatorium / University of the Arts The Hague)
program: Master of Music in Sonology
qualification: Master of Music (MMus), awarded by the Royal Conservatoire The Hague
language: English — 'all lessons are conducted in the English language'
durationEcts: 2 years, 4 semesters (120 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Electronic and computer music, sound synthesis, algorithmic composition, live electronics, sound art, analogue and digital studio practice, artistic research culminating in a thesis and final presentation. Sonology (founded 1960, Utrecht) is the oldest continuously running electronic music institute in Europe.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'The candidate should have a bachelor's diploma relevant for the professional field of Sonology (composition of electronic and/or acoustic music using fixed media, notation, improvisation or some combination of these, sound synthesis research, sound art, related subjects such as artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering, musicology, music perception, film studies, or as a performing musician).'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICIT. The entry text names 'related subjects such as artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering' as relevant bachelor backgrounds. This is one of the very few historic centres that names computer science in writing.
portfolioSpec: QUOTE: 'selected on the basis of a portfolio with previous compositions, sound installations, recordings of live performances or research results in the form of computer programs, articles, theses, etc.' Exact number of works / maximum duration NOT specified on the page — research results (code, articles) count as portfolio items, which is unusually favourable to a software engineer. PLUS a two-page study plan: (1) short description of the proposed project for the master's, (2) a four-semester timeline, (3) detailed project description with central research questions and presentation format, (4) overview of subjects for the final-examination thesis. Plus CV.
auditionSpec: NO LIVE AUDITION. QUOTE: 'There is no live admission exam.' Admission is decided on the submitted portfolio, study plan and CV; decisions made by 1 April. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT FACT IN THIS SWEEP for a candidate who cannot audition on an instrument.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 11,488 per year (institutional tuition fee, University of the Arts The Hague, 2026-2027 rate — PRIOR CYCLE, indexed annually)
otherFees: Statutory fee for EEA is EUR 2,694 by comparison. Dutch visa/residence permit approx. EUR 350; mandatory proof of means approx. EUR 14,000/yr; health insurance.
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 11,500 tuition + approx. EUR 14,000 living = approx. EUR 25,500/yr; approx. EUR 51,000 for the 2-year master
scholarshipName: Excellence Scholarship; NL Scholarship; Top Scholarships; TSH Changemaker Scholarship; Holland Scholarship
scholarships: NL Scholarship explicitly for students from outside the EEA studying in NL for the first time. Excellence Scholarship requires a 9–10 score on the entrance exam. All four have deadline 25 May, awards announced 15 June, letters by 1 July. Amounts NOT published on the page — UNVERIFIED. 'The number of scholarships available is limited.'
languageRequirement: English, adequate fluency expected
englishTest: Required for non-EU/EEA (excluding UK, Canada, Australia, NZ, USA, South Africa): IELTS 6.0 minimum or TOEFL 80; TOEIC or Cambridge English also accepted. Must be submitted before 1 September (i.e. AFTER admission, not before) .
deadline: 26 February 2026 for Sept 2026 entry — PRIOR CYCLE. Expect approx. 26 February 2027 for the September 2027 intake.
applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — typically October/November of the preceding year via Studielink + Conservatoire portal
verdictForCandidate: TOP CANDIDATE. Named computer-science entry route, no live audition, English-taught, historic institution. The only obstacles are the EUR 11,488 fee and the need to build a portfolio (which may include code and written research) by February 2027.

institution: INA-GRM (Groupe de Recherches Musicales, Institut national de l'audiovisuel) — birthplace of musique concrète (Pierre Schaeffer, 1958)
program: Master Création Musicale et Arts Sonores (formerly co-recruited with INA campus) + GRM short training courses (GRM Tools, mastering, etc.)
qualification: NOT A DEGREE IN ITS OWN RIGHT — INA-GRM is a research/production unit of INA and awards no diploma. It contributed to a Bac+5 master delivered by Université Gustave Eiffel. CRITICAL: 'From the 2026 academic year onward, INA campus will no longer participate in recruitment for the Master's programme in musical creation and sonic arts' — INA redirects applicants to Université Gustave Eiffel's new master 'Musiques, Créations, Technologies'. GRM's own offer is short professional stages (a few days), which are NOT degrees.
accreditationStatus: Short courses: no accreditation, French professional-training certificates only. The degree lives at Université Gustave Eiffel.
language: French
durationEcts: Short stages: days to weeks, no ECTS
whatYouStudy: Sound writing and organisation in composition; transformation, manipulation and real-time synthesis; spatialisation in concert (acousmonium); GRM Tools.
entryRequirements: For short courses: professional/continuing-education enrolment, no degree gate. For the master: see the Université Gustave Eiffel record.
acceptsNonMusic: Short courses: yes, open enrolment. UNVERIFIED for any residual master role.
portfolioSpec: None for short courses
auditionSpec: None
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — short courses priced per stage (French continuing-education rates, typically EUR 1,000–3,000 per stage)
otherFees: UNVERIFIED
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED
scholarships: None — continuing education is normally employer-funded in France (does not apply to a foreign student)
languageRequirement: French
deadline: N/A (rolling course enrolment)
verdictForCandidate: NOT A ROUTE. No degree, no student visa, no funding. The GRM legacy is now reachable only through Université Gustave Eiffel's master (next record).

institution: Université Gustave Eiffel (UFR LACT), with INA-GRM, IRCAM, CDMC and École des Beaux-Arts de Bourges as partners
program: Master Musiques, Créations, Technologies (MCT) — parcours: 'Musiques et musicologies', 'Musiques numériques et musicologie computationnelle', 'Production et Performance', 'Création musicale et arts sonores'
qualification: Master (diplôme national de master, Bac+5), awarded by Université Gustave Eiffel
language: French
durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS
whatYouStudy: Depending on parcours: computational musicology and digital music; music production and performance; musical creation and sound arts in the musique concrète / acousmatic tradition (this is the parcours that inherits the INA-GRM lineage). Project-based pedagogy.
entryRequirements: QUOTE (from programme listing): 'Admission is based on a file review and is open to holders of a Licence in music or arts, diploma from a conservatory or art school at equivalent level to L3, or related Masters.'
acceptsNonMusic: PROBLEMATIC — the stated gate is a Licence 'in music or arts' or conservatory/art-school equivalent. A software-engineering BSc is neither. The 'Musiques numériques et musicologie computationnelle' parcours is the only plausible bridge and would need a case-by-case dossier. UNVERIFIED whether they admit science graduates — must be asked directly (master.musique@univ-eiffel.fr).
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — dossier-based; artistic portfolio expected for the 'Création musicale et arts sonores' parcours. Exact spec not published.
auditionSpec: No live audition stated — 'admission is based on a file review' (sur dossier). UNVERIFIED whether an interview follows.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — French public master fee approx. EUR 250/yr, but non-EU 'frais différenciés' of EUR 3,879/yr may apply unless the university exempts (many do). Must be confirmed with the university.
otherFees: CVEC approx. EUR 105/yr
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED; likely EUR 12,000–16,000/yr dominated by Paris-region living costs
scholarshipName: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship (Campus France); Bourse du gouvernement français (BGF) via the French Embassy in Tunis
languageRequirement: French — non-francophone applicants normally need DELF/DALF B2 via Études en France. Candidate is fluent in French: STRONG ADVANTAGE.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — Tunisian applicants must go through the Campus France 'Études en France' procedure, which typically closes in the autumn/winter preceding entry (approx. October–December 2026 for September 2027).
verdictForCandidate: WORTH PURSUING but entry gate says 'Licence in music or arts'. His French fluency and the low French fee structure make this one of the cheapest realistic routes IF they accept a science bachelor. Direct enquiry needed.

institution: CNSMD Lyon — Conservatoire National Supérieur de Musique et de Danse de Lyon
program: Master Composition Électroacoustique (also: Master Composition of Mixed Music; Master Composition for Film & Image; Master Music Theory & Composition)
qualification: Master (2e cycle supérieur), awarded by CNSMD Lyon — a French national conservatoire under the Ministry of Culture; the diploma confers the grade de master
accreditationStatus: State conservatoire, degree confers grade de master
language: French — 'the required French level to enrol in the formation is B1' for music programmes
durationEcts: 4 semesters full-time, 2 years; 'this duration may not be shortened'; attendance mandatory. 120 ECTS.
whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic composition as main discipline — 'the term electroacoustic encompasses a range of approaches and objectives in the field of electronic music, be it accompanied by visual media, theatrical elements, lighting, or none of these, and all forms are welcome'. Studio work, acousmatic writing, mixed music, live electronics, spatialisation.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'Non-graduates of the CNSMD Lyon wishing to enter a Master's (2e cycle) programme must hold a Bachelor's, DNSPM, or equivalent degree from a French or international tertiary education institution IN THE RELEVANT DISCIPLINE.' Age limits stated for the electroacoustic curriculum: candidates aged 16–30.
acceptsNonMusic: NO / VERY UNLIKELY — 'in the relevant discipline' is the operative phrase. A software-engineering BSc is not a degree in electroacoustic composition. He would realistically have to enter the DNSPM (bachelor) level first, or be judged equivalent on the strength of an exceptional portfolio. UNVERIFIED whether the jury exercises discretion.
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED in exact form — application is fully digital on the CNSMD platform 'with the exception of musical scores, which must be sent by mail'; a research project document is required for master entry. Exam programmes published annually (see annales PDF for Cursus Métiers de la Création Musicale).
auditionSpec: YES — there is a competitive entrance examination (concours d'entrée) with published épreuves, held in Lyon on a fixed calendar (Feb–Mar). UNVERIFIED whether any component can be done remotely; French conservatoire concours are normally IN PERSON. This is a serious obstacle for a Tunisian applicant needing a short-stay visa purely to sit the exam.
tuitionNonEU: approx. EUR 500–550 per year — 'Tuition fees at CNSMD Lyon are the same for all students, regardless of their nationality'. NO differentiated non-EU fee. UNVERIFIED to the euro for 2026-27 (study-costs page blocks automated fetch).
otherFees: Entrance exam fee (CROUS scholarship holders exempt); Lyon living approx. EUR 900–1,100/month
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 11,000–14,000/yr, almost all living costs — one of the cheapest elite options in Europe
scholarshipName: CROUS bourses (need-based, limited access for non-EU); Eiffel Excellence Scholarship
languageRequirement: French B1 for music programmes (candidate is fluent — clears this easily)
deadline: Registration for DNSPM and Master entrance exams opened 6 November 2025 and closed 27 November 2025 for the 2026 intake — PRIOR CYCLE. Expect approx. 6–27 November 2026 for the September 2027 intake. 'No late applications will be accepted.'
applicationOpens: Early November of the preceding year, via concours.cnsmd-lyon.fr
verdictForCandidate: Cheapest tuition of any elite centre and French-language (his strength), BUT the entry gate demands a degree 'in the relevant discipline' and a competitive in-person concours. Not realistic for Sept 2027 without prior music credentials. Note the very early deadline: November 2026.

institution: CNSMD Paris — Conservatoire National Supérieur de Musique et de Danse de Paris
program: Composition (1er, 2e et 3e cycles supérieurs), with the 'Nouvelles technologies appliquées à la composition' discipline; 2e cycle 'mixed music' orientation; Composition de Musique à l'Image
qualification: Master (2e cycle supérieur, grade de master), awarded by CNSMD Paris. There is NO standalone electroacoustic-composition master — electroacoustics sits inside the composition curriculum as the 'nouvelles technologies' strand.
language: French
durationEcts: 2 years (2e cycle), 120 ECTS
whatYouStudy: Instrumental composition, computer science and electroacoustic composition, analysis, orchestration, plus compulsory and optional complementary disciplines. Partner of the IRCAM Cursus.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'For admission to the 2nd cycle — mixed music orientation, students must have obtained Certificate B in new technologies as part of the 1st cycle of composition.' Certificate B in New Technologies is ALSO required for the IRCAM programme within the 2e cycle composition. For Composition de Musique à l'Image: 'this cycle is open by competitive exam to students or former students of a musical higher education programme who can justify through the presentation of personal projects significant experience in the field of writing, composition, jazz, or new technologies.'
acceptsNonMusic: NO. The mixed-music master route is effectively internal — it presupposes CNSMDP's own 1st cycle Certificate B. The film-music route requires 'students or former students of a musical higher education programme'. A software-engineering BSc does not qualify.
portfolioSpec: Personal projects/works must be presented; exact spec UNVERIFIED
auditionSpec: YES — competitive entrance exam (concours). 'The admission process involves a presentation of the Master's programme, work, and project, followed by an interview lasting a maximum of 45 minutes.' In person in Paris. UNVERIFIED whether remote is possible.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — CNSMDP charges modest French public fees (historically approx. EUR 500/yr), same for all nationalities. Must confirm.
otherFees: Paris living approx. EUR 1,200–1,500/month
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED
languageRequirement: French (level UNVERIFIED; B2 typical)
deadline: UNVERIFIED — CNSMDP concours registration typically closes in the winter (Dec–Feb) preceding the September intake
verdictForCandidate: CLOSED. The electroacoustic strand is a certificate inside an internal composition pipeline, not an open master. Rule out.

institution: ARTS² — Conservatoire Royal de Mons (École Supérieure des Arts). Section d'électroacoustique founded by Annette Vande Gorne; the only such teaching in Belgium.
program: Master à finalité spécialisée en Musique — option Composition acousmatique (also: Composition appliquée aux multimédias / Musiques appliquées; Composition)
qualification: Master à finalité spécialisée (120 ECTS over Bachelor+Master five-year structure), awarded by ARTS² / Conservatoire Royal de Mons, Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles
accreditationStatus: Accredited Belgian higher-arts degree (École Supérieure des Arts, FWB); Bologna-compliant since 2002
language: FRENCH — teaching is in French. This is a major advantage for a francophone Tunisian.
durationEcts: Master: 2 years / 120 ECTS. The acousmatic composition training is described as a five-year path (bachelor 180 + master 120).
whatYouStudy: Acousmatic composition — 'music composed in studio from recorded sounds rather than by writing notes on a score'; listening/analysis (Schaefferian typo-morphology), spatialisation and acousmonium performance, multimedia applied composition, studio technique. Teachers include Sophie Delafontaine, Julien Guillamat, Daniel Perez Hajdu, Roald Baudoux, Elizabeth Anderson, Fabian Balthazart.
entryRequirements: For master entry: 'candidates must submit a letter of motivation to the director describing their specialised artistic project, and depending on the discipline, an examination of aptitude may be requested.' Non-EU applicants must supply passport, secondary-education certificate with an equivalence request filed with the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, prior artistic training records, documentation of the last five years of activity, and an attestation of no outstanding debts.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED but MORE OPEN THAN THE FRENCH CONSERVATOIRES — the master admission text does not require a music degree by name; it requires a motivation letter with a specialised artistic project and an aptitude exam. NOTE: entry at BACHELOR (bac1) level is genuinely open to non-musicians and may be the honest route here. Must be confirmed with the school.
portfolioSpec: For composers (from the school's own international/master guidance): 'At least three (preferably four)' composition scores WITH audio recordings. For acousmatic candidates, works are fixed-media, so recordings substitute for scores. Exact durations UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: YES, THERE IS AN ADMISSION EXAM, but its content is unusually favourable to a non-performer: for the composition acousmatique option the exam includes 'a written test of perceptive abilities (comparing 2 or 3 electroacoustic sequences to define their similarities or differences)' and 'a perceptual description of an excerpt from a work heard twice'. IT IS A LISTENING TEST, NOT AN INSTRUMENTAL AUDITION. Admission exams are organised each year in MAY and SEPTEMBER. UNVERIFIED whether they can be sat remotely — assume in-person in Mons.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,194 annual registration fee + EUR 4,175 mandatory supplementary contribution for non-EU students = EUR 5,369/year. EXEMPTION from the EUR 4,175 supplement for UN Least Developed Countries, FWB secondary graduates, or holders of a Wallonie-Bruxelles International (WBI) scholarship. TUNISIA IS NOT AN LDC, so the supplement applies unless he wins a WBI grant.
otherFees: EUR 50 minimum deposit by 15 Sept 2026; balance by 15 Jan 2027. Diploma equivalence request via www.equivalences.cfwb.be — 'Les demandes d'équivalence sont clôturées au 15 juillet' (hard deadline, postal only, notarised translations required). Belgian residence permit; living approx. EUR 800–1,000/month in Mons (cheap).
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 5,369 fees + approx. EUR 10,000 living = approx. EUR 15,400/yr; approx. EUR 1,194 + living if WBI-funded
scholarshipName: MASTER IN — Wallonie-Bruxelles International (WBI) scholarships for international master's students
scholarships: WBI 'MASTER IN' grants: applicants must 'hold a recognised Bachelor's degree issued by the competent authorities of their country, obtained no more than five (5) years before' the programme start. Application deadline 31 March 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE) via forms.office.com; see studyinbelgium.be/fr/bourse-master-wbi. A WBI grant ALSO exempts the EUR 4,175 supplement — double benefit. Contact service.erasmus@artsaucarre.be.
languageRequirement: French (no test stated on the pages seen — UNVERIFIED)
deadline: Admission exams in MAY and SEPTEMBER each year. Equivalence dossier closes 15 JULY (hard). WBI MASTER IN scholarship deadline 31 March 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE; expect 31 March 2027 for a Sept 2027 start.
verdictForCandidate: STRONG CANDIDATE — arguably the best francophone option. The admission test is a LISTENING/PERCEPTION test rather than an instrumental audition; teaching is in French; fees are moderate and a WBI scholarship both funds him and waives the non-EU supplement. Historic lineage (Vande Gorne, direct descendant of the Schaefferian school).

institution: Musiques & Recherches / Studios Métamorphoses d'Orphée (founded 1982 by Annette Vande Gorne)
program: Métamorphoses international acousmatic composition competition; Espace du son spatialised-performance competition; international summer workshops on spatialisation (since 1999) and on electroacoustic composition (since 1987); L'Espace du son festival; Electrodoc documentation centre
qualification: NOT A DEGREE — an independent non-profit studio, competition organiser and summer-workshop provider. It awards no diploma and enrols no degree students.

durationEcts: Workshops of days to two weeks; no ECTS
whatYouStudy: Acousmatic composition, spatialisation and acousmonium interpretation, Schaefferian listening
entryRequirements: Open enrolment for workshops; competitions open to composers internationally
acceptsNonMusic: Yes for workshops (no degree gate)
portfolioSpec: For the Métamorphoses competition: a fixed-media acousmatic work (spec varies by edition — UNVERIFIED for 2026/2027)
auditionSpec: None
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — workshop fees per session
otherFees: UNVERIFIED
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED
languageRequirement: French useful
deadline: Competition deadlines vary by edition
verdictForCandidate: NOT A DEGREE, but STRATEGICALLY USEFUL: its summer workshops are a fast, cheap way to build the acousmatic portfolio and the Vande Gorne connection that ARTS² Mons admission would reward. Treat as a portfolio-building step in 2026, not a destination.

institution: Le Fresnoy — Studio national des arts contemporains
program: Two-year post-diploma course in contemporary arts (film, video, sound creation, electronic sound production, interactive audio, immersive environments)
qualification: 'The diploma of the Fresnoy-Studio national des arts contemporains' — an establishment diploma under the Ministry of Culture (Direction Générale de la Création Artistique). WHETHER IT CARRIES THE GRADE DE MASTER / RNCP LEVEL 7 IS UNVERIFIED — the official admissions page does not state it.
accreditationStatus: Ministry of Culture supervision; master-level equivalence UNVERIFIED
language: French — 'the course itself is conducted in French'; 'Candidates must have knowledge of spoken French and English'
durationEcts: 2 years; no ECTS stated
whatYouStudy: Year 1: film, photography, video, SOUND CREATION and music creation, cross-disciplinary experimentation. Year 2: digital creation — interactive video/audio, ELECTRONIC SOUND PRODUCTION, programmed audio, animation, immersive environments. Visiting professors have included Atau Tanaka, Georges Aperghis and Ryoji Ikeda.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'aged 35 years maximum on 1st January of the current year, born after 31st December 1990'. Plus EITHER 'A levels/Baccalauréat plus 5 years of validated study' OR 'A levels/Baccalauréat plus 7 years of artistic/professional experience (minimum age 24)'.
acceptsNonMusic: YES in principle — 'designed for students across a wide range of artistic fields (visual arts, cinema, photography, video, architecture, music, performing arts, etc.) from all types of educational backgrounds and of all nationalities'. BUT the Bac+5 requirement is a hard gate for a 3-year BSc holder: he would have to qualify under the Bac+7-years-of-artistic/professional-experience route, and software engineering work is unlikely to be counted as artistic experience. RISK.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: one video file, MP4, MAXIMUM 8 MINUTES, containing work samples; background summary (10 lines max); motivation letter (3-page PDF); project proposals for the 2-year programme (1 page per project); list of inspiring artists/works (20 lines); administrative documents (portrait, ID copy, CV).
auditionSpec: NO PERFORMANCE AUDITION. Two-stage: (1) dossier/portfolio preselection, (2) INTERVIEW for up to 60 candidates. CRUCIALLY: 'Non-European applicants may participate via video conference for interviews.' Interviews 18–22 May 2026.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 760 per year for 2026-2027 (same for all; 'with the exception of registration fees, studies are free for all students')
otherFees: Living in Tourcoing/Lille approx. EUR 800–1,000/month; production costs of student films are FUNDED BY LE FRESNOY (a significant hidden benefit)
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 760 + approx. EUR 10,000–12,000 living = approx. EUR 11,000–13,000/yr
scholarshipName: UNVERIFIED — production budgets are provided; separate living stipends UNVERIFIED
languageRequirement: Spoken French AND English required; course in French. No test stated.
deadline: Portfolio deadline 11 March 2026, 15:00 Paris time — PRIOR CYCLE. Preselection results 20 April 2026; interviews 18–22 May 2026; final results 25 May 2026. Expect approx. 11 March 2027 for a September 2027 start.
verdictForCandidate: EXTREMELY ATTRACTIVE on cost (EUR 760/yr), language (French), remote video interview for non-Europeans, and production funding — but only 24 places a year, a Bac+5 entry gate he does not meet, and an 8-minute portfolio video he does not yet have. Long-shot; also the degree level is unverified, which matters for visa and later study.

city: Tallinn — Stockholm — Lyon — Hamburg (one semester each)
institution: Consortium: Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre (EAMT) + Royal College of Music Stockholm (KMH) + CNSMD Lyon + Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (HfMT)
program: CoPeCo — MA in Contemporary Performance and Composition
qualification: 'An artistic master's degree from your home institution, along with a certificate signed by the vice-chancellors of the participating institutions' — i.e. a degree from whichever consortium member is the student's home institution, plus a joint certificate
accreditationStatus: Accredited in each partner country; joint consortium programme
institutionType: Consortium of four state conservatoires/music universities
language: English (B1 required)
durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS. Mobility: Sem 1 EAMT Tallinn (Sep–Jan), Sem 2 KMH Stockholm (Jan–Jun), Sem 3 CNSMD Lyon (Sep–Feb), Sem 4 HfMT Hamburg (Apr–Sep).
whatYouStudy: Experimental contemporary performance and composition — live electronics, improvisation, interdisciplinary and cross-arts practice, 'an open platform for experimental artistic practice within a European setting'.
entryRequirements: EAMT: 'Applicants with at least a Bachelors degree in music or equivalent or in the final year of their undergraduate studies are eligible.' KMH is stricter: 'a Degree of Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music (180 credits)' and 'A music bachelor degree is explicitly required.' Documents: Bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) + diploma supplement, transcripts, proof of English B1.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — a music bachelor (or 'equivalent') is required. The 'or equivalent' clause is the only opening and would need an exceptional portfolio. This is a real barrier for a software-engineering BSc.
portfolioSpec: EXACT. Composers: MINIMUM THREE contrasting original compositions totalling AT LEAST 15 MINUTES (scores and/or recordings). Performers: minimum two contrasting performance excerpts, at least 15 minutes total. Composer/performers: one original composition, one performance recording, plus another work, totalling at least 15 minutes.
auditionSpec: AUDITION IS ONLINE — 'The audition is conducted online and includes: presentation of work (max 20 minutes), improvisation test, and interview discussing the Masters Degree Project proposal. All auditions will be recorded, and if there are more successful applicants than study places the recordings will be evaluated by a joint international panel.' NO TRAVEL REQUIRED. Note the IMPROVISATION TEST — this requires live musical ability.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — not published on the EAMT or KMH CoPeCo pages. KMH normally charges non-EU/EEA students a tuition fee; EAMT and CNSMD Lyon are low-fee. Must be confirmed with the consortium (hanneleen.pihlak@eamt.ee).
otherFees: Four relocations across four Schengen/EU countries in two years — residence-permit costs in Estonia, Sweden, France and Germany. Administratively heavy for a Tunisian national.
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED
scholarshipName: UNVERIFIED — was formerly Erasmus Mundus-funded; current scholarship status UNVERIFIED
languageRequirement: English B1 — 'Proof of English language skills (B1): IELTS, TOEFL or equivalent'
englishTest: IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent at B1 — an unusually LOW English bar
deadline: BIENNIAL ADMISSION — 'Admission every other year, 1 December – 15 January'. KMH states 'No admissions to autumn 2026'. THE NEXT INTAKE IS AUTUMN 2027, with applications expected OPEN 1 DECEMBER 2026 – 31 JANUARY 2027. THIS IS EXACTLY THE CANDIDATE'S CYCLE.
verdictForCandidate: TIMING IS PERFECT (biennial, next intake Sept 2027) and the AUDITION IS ONLINE with a low English bar. But it demands a music bachelor, three original compositions of 15+ minutes, and an improvisation test — it is aimed at trained performer-composers. Keep on the list only if he can build a real portfolio in 2026.

institution: HfG Karlsruhe (Staatliche Hochschule für Gestaltung), founded 1992 alongside ZKM
program: Media Art (Medienkunst) — with the 'Sound' study focus (medienkunst-sound.de), led by Prof. Paul Modler and Lorenz Schwarz
qualification: NOT A MASTER — HfG awards a DIPLOM (9 semesters, described by the school as 'comparable to a Master's degree') in Media Art, and a Magister in Art Research and Media Philosophy. There is no separate 2-year master to enter with a bachelor.
accreditationStatus: State art university (Baden-Württemberg); Diplom is a recognised German degree but is a long single-cycle award, not a Bologna master
institutionType: Public university of arts and design
language: German — DSH-1, TestDaF TDN 3+, or Goethe-Zertifikat B2 or higher required for international applicants
durationEcts: Diplom: 9 semesters (4.5 years). Winter semester start only.
whatYouStudy: 'Electronic music and its aesthetic history, DIY and experimental approaches to sound, spatial sound, and the relations between traditional musical practices and contemporary art.' Sound sits inside Media Art.
entryRequirements: 'General or subject-specific higher education entrance qualification as well as successful completion of the admission procedure, including the assessment of academic and/or artistic aptitude', plus an interview determining professional or artistic aptitude.
acceptsNonMusic: YES in principle (art-school aptitude model, no music degree named) — but the award is a 9-semester Diplom starting from scratch, not a postgraduate master.
portfolioSpec: Artistic portfolio is decisive: 'Admission is based on the application portfolio, where the artistic portfolio is of most importance for praxis-based subjects.' Exact number/format varies annually — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: No performance audition, but an INTERVIEW for determining artistic aptitude is part of the admission procedure. Location/remote option UNVERIFIED.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,500 per semester for non-EU/EEA citizens = EUR 3,000 per year
otherFees: Semester fee EUR 202.50 per semester (approx. EUR 405/yr). Certified German/English translations of certificates required.
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 3,400 fees + approx. EUR 11,000 living = approx. EUR 14,400/yr, over 4.5 years
scholarships: UNVERIFIED at institution level; HfG notes the possible future abolition of international student tuition is under government discussion
languageRequirement: German B2 / TestDaF 3 / DSH-1 REQUIRED. The candidate has no German — this is a hard block for a 2027 start.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — winter-semester intake only; see hfg-karlsruhe.de/studium/bewerbung/bewerbungsverfahren/
verdictForCandidate: RULE OUT for 2027: no master's (Diplom only), German B2 required, and EUR 3,000/yr non-EU tuition. The Sound focus is genuinely excellent but the structure does not fit a bachelor-holder seeking a 2-year master.

institution: Technische Universität Berlin — Audio Communication Group / Elektronisches Studio der TU Berlin (founded 1953, one of the oldest electronic studios in Europe)
program: M.Sc. Audio Communication and Technology (Audiokommunikation und -technologie). The Elektronisches Studio is a facility of this group, not a separate degree.
qualification: Master of Science (M.Sc.), awarded by TU Berlin
language: GERMAN is the main language of instruction. 'The main language of instruction in the Master's programme is German. If you are applying with foreign qualifications, you will therefore have to prove German skills at level C1 for admission.' Plus English B2 for literature.
durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS
whatYouStudy: Audio technology, psychoacoustics, music acoustics, spatial audio, music information retrieval, electronic music studio practice, sound reinforcement, systematic musicology.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'a first university degree in a science, engineering, humanities, social science, arts, business or law programme, or an equivalent teaching degree.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY — a science or engineering first degree qualifies. No music degree needed, no portfolio.
portfolioSpec: No artistic portfolio required — this is a technical M.Sc.
auditionSpec: NO AUDITION AT ALL. Admission is by academic record.
tuitionNonEU: No tuition fee at TU Berlin (Berlin charges no tuition for non-EU students); semester fee only, approx. EUR 350–400 per semester (UNVERIFIED exact 2026-27 amount)
otherFees: Blocked account for visa: approx. EUR 11,904/yr (German requirement, UNVERIFIED for 2027); health insurance approx. EUR 130/month
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 800 fees + approx. EUR 12,000–14,000 living = approx. EUR 13,000–15,000/yr
languageRequirement: GERMAN C1 — HARD BLOCK for this candidate (no German). Would require roughly 2 years of intensive German study.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — TU Berlin master deadlines for international applicants are typically 15 January (winter) via uni-assist
verdictForCandidate: PERFECT ACADEMIC FIT (accepts an engineering bachelor, no audition, no tuition) BUT BLOCKED BY GERMAN C1. If he were willing to spend 2026-27 learning German, this becomes one of the best-value options in Europe. Note the linked joint route in the next record.

institution: TU Berlin (Audio Communication Group) + Institute of Sonology, Royal Conservatoire The Hague
program: Audio Communication and Sonology — joint master's route
qualification: Master of Music in Sonology from the Royal Conservatoire The Hague (plus the TU Berlin M.Sc. track). Students 'apply for the master's programme Audio Communication and Technology at the TU Berlin first; until 15 February of the following year they can apply for a change to The Hague.'
language: English emphasised on the Sonology side; 'No German language requirement is explicitly mentioned. The emphasis is on good knowledge of English.' NOTE: this CONTRADICTS TU Berlin's own C1 German rule for the M.Sc. — the contradiction is UNRESOLVED and must be checked with both institutions.
durationEcts: Programme starts in October; transfer to The Hague requested by 15 February of the following year
whatYouStudy: Audio communication/technology at TU Berlin combined with Sonology's artistic electronic-music training
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'Bachelor's, master's, or graduate degree in science, engineering, humanities, social sciences, artistic-scientific studies, business, or law from a German or foreign university'; 'Proficiency in English'; 'Strong foundation in higher mathematics (calculus, linear algebra)'; 'Knowledge of a programming language or computer algebra system'.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY ENGINEERING/SCIENCE FRIENDLY, and it actively REQUIRES programming and higher mathematics. A software-engineering BSc is close to the ideal profile for this route.
portfolioSpec: Not addressed on the joint page — UNVERIFIED. Presumably the Sonology portfolio applies at the transfer stage.
auditionSpec: None stated. Sonology's own rule ('There is no live admission exam') presumably governs the Hague side.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED for the joint route — TU Berlin charges no tuition; the Hague side would charge the institutional non-EEA fee (EUR 11,488/yr) unless the exchange arrangement waives it. MUST BE CLARIFIED.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED
languageRequirement: Contradiction unresolved — 'good knowledge of English' per the Sonology page vs German C1 per TU Berlin's admission rules
deadline: Transfer application to The Hague by 15 February of the year following entry; TU Berlin's own master deadline applies first
verdictForCandidate: HIGH-VALUE LEAD WITH ONE UNRESOLVED QUESTION. On paper this is the single best-matched entry requirement found in the whole sweep (engineering degree + programming + maths, English), but the German-language contradiction has to be resolved by email before it can be relied on.

institution: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln) — home of the Studio für Elektronische Musik, successor to the legendary WDR Studio of Stockhausen
program: Master of Music Elektronische Komposition (Electronic Composition). A Bachelor of Music in Elektronische Komposition also exists.
qualification: Master of Music (M.Mus.), awarded by HfMT Köln
institutionType: Public university of music and dance
language: German (instruction). Language proof unusually lenient — see below.
durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS
whatYouStudy: Electronic composition in the WDR-studio lineage; concert music plus theatre, video, installation and performance — 'the field of work of today's composers has expanded considerably'.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'Successful completion of a four-year bachelor's degree in composition or equivalent.' DAAD phrasing: 'A prerequisite for the Master's degree in Electronic Composition is the completion of a Bachelor's degree in Composition or a comparable course of study. Specialized previous studies in the field of electronics are not necessary.'
acceptsNonMusic: NO — a bachelor 'in composition or equivalent' is required, and it must be FOUR YEARS. A 3-year Tunisian BSc in software engineering fails on both counts. The Bachelor of Music in Elektronische Komposition would be the honest entry point instead.
portfolioSpec: Own works must be submitted for the colloquium; exact number/format is set in the Eignungsprüfungsordnung — UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: QUOTE: 'a colloquium with the presentation and discussion of submitted works, with questions about the candidate's own musical aesthetics and prior knowledge in the field of contemporary music.' NO instrumental audition. Whether the colloquium is in person in Cologne or remote is UNVERIFIED.
tuitionNonEU: No tuition fee (NRW charges none); semester fee approx. EUR 300–400 per semester = approx. EUR 600–800/yr
otherFees: Visa blocked account, health insurance
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 700 fees + approx. EUR 11,000–12,000 living = approx. EUR 12,000/yr — very cheap
languageRequirement: REMARKABLY LOW: for Master programmes, 'proof of at least language proficiency level A2 must be submitted BY THE END OF THE FIRST SEMESTER' for applicants who did not obtain their qualification at a German-speaking institution. No German is needed at application. (Bachelor requires B2 by end of second semester.)
deadline: 1 MARCH each year for the following winter semester, via the muvac.com portal. So approx. 1 March 2027 for October 2027 entry.
verdictForCandidate: The German-language bar is the LOWEST of any German institution found (A2 after arrival, nothing at application), tuition is effectively free, and the entrance test is a colloquium about your own works rather than an audition. The blocker is the 'four-year bachelor's degree in composition' requirement. Worth an email asking whether an exceptional portfolio can substitute.

institution: Folkwang Universität der Künste — ICEM, Institut für Computermusik und Elektronische Medien (founded 1990, the university's oldest cross-faculty institute)
program: Integrative Komposition (M.Mus.) — four artistic focus areas including ELEKTRONISCHE KOMPOSITION (also instrumental composition, composition and visualisation). A B.Mus. of the same name exists.
qualification: Master of Music (M.Mus.), awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste
accreditationStatus: State-accredited German university of the arts
language: German instruction. 'Most classes are taught in German.'
durationEcts: 4 semesters full-time (part-time possible), 120 ECTS
whatYouStudy: Integrative composition across instrumental composition, electronic composition, and composition-and-visualisation; ICEM studios, computer music, electronic media.
entryRequirements: QUOTE: 'First university degree' AND 'Evidence of artistic aptitude or outstanding artistic talent' demonstrated through the two-stage aptitude test. NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: it does NOT say the first degree must be in music or composition.
acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY YES — the stated gate is 'first university degree' + artistic aptitude, with no subject restriction. This is materially more open than HfMT Köln ('bachelor in composition') or CNSMD Lyon ('in the relevant discipline'). Should be confirmed by email, but on the published wording a software-engineering BSc is not excluded.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: 'own works in the form of original scores (especially for CAS instrumental composition), recordings, videos etc.' in PDF or MP4, 'ideally under 25 MB but not exceeding 100 MB'; larger files may be linked via a video platform or cloud storage. PLUS a project plan/concept 'describing the topics and intended results of artistic engagement during master studies'. Plus the application form.
auditionSpec: TWO-STAGE, first stage REMOTE. Stage 1: 'conducted digitally and consists of submitting a portfolio with own compositions and a draft for the master project electronically (via file link)'. Stage 2 (only if stage 1 is passed): approximately 30 MINUTES IN PERSON, a colloquium on the submitted works. NO instrumental audition. Only one trip to Essen, and only if shortlisted.
tuitionNonEU: NO TUITION CHARGED. 'no tuition charged. Semester fees cover student union services, student committee work, and transit pass.' Semester fee amount UNVERIFIED (NRW norm approx. EUR 300/semester, includes a regional transport ticket).
otherFees: EUR 50 application fee. Visa blocked account, health insurance.
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 650 fees + approx. EUR 10,000–11,000 living = approx. EUR 11,000/yr. Among the cheapest master's in this sweep.
languageRequirement: German B1 — 'proof of language level B1 with enrolment', i.e. by enrolment, NOT at application. Achievable in about a year of study from zero.
deadline: 15 MARCH for the winter semester; 15 NOVEMBER for the summer semester. For a winter-2027/28 start: 15 March 2027. (The 15 March 2026 deadline was for winter 2026/27 — PRIOR CYCLE.)
verdictForCandidate: ONE OF THE FIVE STRONGEST FINDS. Entry requirement is just 'first university degree' + artistic aptitude; no tuition; portfolio is digital; only the shortlisted second round is in person; German only B1 and only by enrolment. The work needed is the portfolio plus about a year of German.

institution: Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (HfMT Hamburg)
program: Multimedia Composition (Multimediale Komposition), M.A. — directed by Prof. Alexander Schubert and Prof. Dr. George Hajdu. HfMT Hamburg is also the semester-4 host of CoPeCo.
qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.), awarded by HfMT Hamburg
accreditationStatus: State-accredited German university of music and theatre
institutionType: Public university of music and theatre
language: The entrance examination and presentation are IN ENGLISH; the programme is English-facing. BUT the institution's general rule states German B2 is required for admission to any bachelor's or master's for applicants without a German Abitur — whether Multimedia Composition is exempt is UNVERIFIED and must be confirmed with studium@hfmt.hamburg.de.
durationEcts: 2 years (master only — no corresponding bachelor). ECTS UNVERIFIED (presumably 120).
whatYouStudy: Algorithmic composition, live electronics, GAME ENGINE DEVELOPMENT, video and light programming, digital studio work; 'interactivity and performance, such as live interaction between music and video, network-based composition, sensor-driven systems, and interactive installations'. Since 2010 graduates can continue to an artistic doctorate (Dr. scientiae musicae).
entryRequirements: 'The prerequisite for studying at the HfMT HH is successful participation in the artistic and academic entrance examination for the desired course of study.' No named prior-degree subject on the exam page — UNVERIFIED whether a music bachelor is formally required.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED but the profile is unusually programming-heavy (Max/MSP, game engines, sensors), which suits a software engineer. The exam itself tests MAX/MSP fundamentals and electronic-music history rather than instrumental skill.
portfolioSpec: EXACT: 'three (electronic / multimedia) works of yours' to be presented, 'ideally with a slideshow and audio/video excerpts'.
auditionSpec: NO INSTRUMENTAL AUDITION, but a real two-part examination: (1) a WRITTEN EXAM of 3 HOURS — 'Multiple Choice Theory' on electronic music basics, history, and MAX/MSP fundamentals, plus a 'Written Text' section requiring the candidate to 'Design a small multimedia artwork (as a concept on paper)' and analyse a provided text; (2) a 15-MINUTE ORAL PRESENTATION of three works with excerpts, followed by Q&A. 'The exam and presentation are in English.' Exam dates for the 2026 cycle: 27–28 April 2026. Whether it can be sat remotely is UNVERIFIED — a 3-hour written paper suggests in person in Hamburg.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — Hamburg charges no tuition for state universities; semester fee applies (approx. EUR 350/semester). Must confirm.
otherFees: Application fee UNVERIFIED; visa blocked account; health insurance
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — likely approx. EUR 13,000–15,000/yr, mostly living costs (Hamburg is expensive)
languageRequirement: Contradiction: exam in English, but institutional rule says German B2. MUST BE RESOLVED.
deadline: Application period for winter semester 2026/27: 15 February 2026 to 1 April 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE. Expect approx. 15 Feb – 1 April 2027 for a winter 2027/28 start. Entrance exam late April.
verdictForCandidate: VERY STRONG CONTENT MATCH — an English-language exam that tests Max/MSP and concept design rather than instrumental performance, and a curriculum built on programming and game engines. The two open questions are the German B2 institutional rule and whether the 3-hour written exam can be sat remotely.

verdictForCandidate: English-taught and historically important, and the full-tuition scholarship is a genuine funding path — but it demands a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music and a probably-in-person March exam. Apply only with a strong portfolio and after confirming the scholarship mechanism and remote-exam possibility.

whatYouStudy: Electronic Composition (Aarhus): 'The target audience of the programme is composers who want to work professionally with the composition and production of electronic music.' Electronic Music Production (Aalborg): aimed at producers wanting to 'work professionally with electronic music production' and 'complete commercial and diverse professional electronic music production assignments' — THIS SECOND ONE IS THE CLOSEST THING IN EUROPE TO A DEGREE FOR AN ELECTRONIC-MUSIC PRODUCER.
entryRequirements: QUOTE from the official 2026/27 admission-requirements PDF: 'To be admitted to a master's programme at RAMA, applicants must have earned a relevant bachelor's degree or earn such a degree before starting on the master's programme. The following bachelor's degrees are PRE-APPROVED: Bachelor's degree from a music academy; Bachelor's degree from another artistic programme approved by the Danish Ministry of Culture*; Bachelor's degree from a university musicology programme*.' Footnote: '*The applicant may have to pass an extended admission test to verify that he/she possesses the skills, knowledge, or qualifications that are acquired on music academy bachelor programmes but which the applicant may not have acquired on his/her qualifying BA programme. Examples include ear training, music theory, general music skills, minor instruments, or technical disciplines.'
acceptsNonMusic: NOT PRE-APPROVED, BUT NOT EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED. The wording is 'a relevant bachelor's degree', followed by a list of PRE-APPROVED degrees — which implies other degrees are assessed case by case, possibly with an extended admission test. Given the electronic-production programme's professional (not conservatoire) orientation, a direct enquiry is warranted.
portfolioSpec: EXACT, from the official PDF. ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION (Aarhus): 'The applicant uploads a MAXIMUM OF 20 MINUTES OF MUSIC featuring works composed and produced by the applicant with the application form. The works can be cross-disciplinary and include video. Information about production location, equipment used, and any other participants must be clear.' Plus an application form covering motivation, expectations, ambitions after the programme, 'the applicant's familiarity with relevant hardware and software', work descriptions, education so far, artistic experience, and experience as a music communicator/teacher, with diplomas attached. ELECTRONIC MUSIC PRODUCTION (Aalborg): '15-20 MINUTES OF AUDIO featuring works produced by the applicant… The applicant is encouraged to demonstrate artistic coherence and at the same time a degree of variation'; plus a work description of 'maximum of two A4 pages' explaining the background of the music and how it was created; plus a CV emphasising music-production experience; plus the bachelor diploma.
auditionSpec: NO INSTRUMENTAL AUDITION — this is a portfolio-plus-interview model. ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION: works are evaluated by a board of examiners; shortlisted applicants are invited to an interview and 'will receive a SET ASSIGNMENT from the board of examiners prior to the interview'. Interview lasts approx. 25 minutes: applicant gives a presentation of MAXIMUM 7 MINUTES on software/hardware used, own artistic practice and ambitions; then 'the composition assignment is played back (2 minutes)' and the applicant explains it (4 minutes); then dialogue with the panel. 'The interview emphasises the applicant's capacity for aesthetic reflection, his/her ability to use electronics in an artistic context, and the applicant's general suitability for study.' Total 25 min + 20 min evaluation/feedback. ELECTRONIC MUSIC PRODUCTION: 'No later than 8 days prior to the admission test, the applicants receive a production assignment' — test is a 10-minute presentation plus a 20-minute interview, maximum 30 minutes. WHETHER THE INTERVIEW CAN BE DONE ONLINE IS UNVERIFIED (RAMA does allow non-EU bachelor applicants to upload 'an unedited video recording (one take)' instead of attending, which suggests remote accommodation exists — must be confirmed for master's).
tuitionNonEU: CONFLICTING FIGURES — Study in Denmark states EUR 6,600 PER TERM (approx. EUR 13,200/yr) for non-EU/EEA/CH; another source states DKK 114,578 per year (approx. EUR 15,350). EU/EEA/CH students pay EUR 0. MUST BE CONFIRMED with RAMA. Half-fee (DKK 29,348 per semester) applies only to certain postgraduate ensemble diplomas.
otherFees: Application fee DKK 500 (approx. EUR 67), non-refundable, 'contributes to the cost of admission tests'. Danish residence permit; living approx. DKK 8,000–10,000/month.
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 13,200–15,400 tuition + approx. EUR 12,000 living = approx. EUR 25,000–27,500/yr
scholarshipName: UNVERIFIED — Danish Cultural Ministry institutions have very limited scholarship provision for non-EU students
languageRequirement: No language test named in the admission-requirements document — UNVERIFIED
deadline: APPLICATION DEADLINE 1 DECEMBER at 12.00 noon (for the 2026/27 year it was 1 December 2025). Admission tests scheduled for JANUARY AND FEBRUARY. For non-EU/EEA applicants the application system opened 3 December 2025 for the following cycle. FOR A SEPTEMBER 2027 START THE DEADLINE IS APPROXIMATELY 1 DECEMBER 2026 — one of the earliest in this whole sweep.
verdictForCandidate: ONE OF THE FIVE BEST FINDS. The admission test is literally: submit 15–20 minutes of your own electronic music, do a set production assignment, then talk for 25 minutes about your gear, your process and your ambitions. There is no instrumental audition, no score-reading, no music-theory paper. The Aalborg 'Electronic Music Production' master in particular is aimed at exactly what he wants to become. The obstacles are the non-pre-approved bachelor and the EUR 13,000+ non-EU fee with no confirmed scholarship.

institution: Sibelius Academy, University of the Arts Helsinki (Uniarts) — Centre for Music & Technology
program: Music Technology, master's programme (a combined Bachelor+Master route also exists)
qualification: Master of Music, awarded by the University of the Arts Helsinki
language: 'The languages of tuition in the Music Technology programme are Finnish, Swedish, and English. The status of English is very pronounced within the Music Technology programme.'
durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS (preliminary study plan of max 150 ECTS is requested at application)
whatYouStudy: Music technology, studio and live sound, electronic composition and production, sound design, music informatics
entryRequirements: QUOTE: applicants must have 'A lower university degree in music (Bachelor)' or equivalent — BUT with an explicit exception: 'a higher education degree in the field of TECHNOLOGY or media is also applicable IF YOU ALSO HAVE A SUFFICIENT AMOUNT OF MUSIC STUDIES.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES, CONDITIONALLY — a technology degree is expressly admissible, but only 'if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies'. A software-engineering BSc with no formal music study fails the second half of the condition as written. Whether self-taught practice counts is UNVERIFIED and must be asked (siba.admissions@uniarts.fi).
portfolioSpec: EXACT: 'a maximum of three works, and at least one of them must be a sound or audiovisual recording'. Combined portfolio and video presentation must NOT EXCEED 10 MINUTES TOTAL. Files must be MP3 (audio) or MP4 (video, H.264/x.264). Plus: project descriptions, motivation letter, CV, final project plan, and a preliminary study plan (max 150 ECTS).
auditionSpec: FULLY REMOTE — 'All assessment components occur via remote connection.' Two stages: (1) advance assignments / portfolio evaluation, (2) a LIVE entrance exam (audition and interview) conducted REMOTELY (30 March – 1 April 2026 in the prior cycle). 'No on-site attendance in Helsinki is required.' EXCELLENT for a visa-needing candidate.
tuitionNonEU: EUR 28,000 PER ACADEMIC YEAR for students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland studying in English, for those starting August 2026 or later.
otherFees: Living in Helsinki approx. EUR 900–1,200/month; Finnish residence permit
totalCostEstimate: approx. EUR 28,000 + approx. EUR 12,000 living = approx. EUR 40,000/yr, approx. EUR 80,000 for the degree
scholarships: CRITICAL: 'The university does not grant any scholarships to cover the tuition fee for students starting in August 2026 or later' and 'there is no waiver programme for students starting 1.8.2026 or later.' The former 50% waiver applies only to students who began before 1 August 2026. THIS EFFECTIVELY RULES THE PROGRAMME OUT ON COST.
languageRequirement: Proficiency in Finnish, Swedish or English must be demonstrated before the application deadline, via prior degree study or a standardised test
englishTest: Standardised test accepted; the language certificate deadline in the prior cycle was 2 March 2026
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE: application period 7 January 2026 08:00 – 21 January 2026 15:00 EET; supporting documents by 28 January 2026; remote entrance exam 30 March – 1 April 2026. FOR THE CANDIDATE'S CYCLE: 'The next possible time to apply is in JANUARY 2027, with studies beginning in AUGUST 2027.' The admissions guide 'will be updated on this page in October–November 2026.'
verdictForCandidate: PERFECT PROCESS, IMPOSSIBLE PRICE. The only fully-remote entrance examination found in this sweep, an English-heavy programme, a technology-degree exception in the entry rules, and the intake falls exactly on his cycle (apply January 2027, start August 2027). But EUR 28,000/year with NO scholarships and NO waivers for anyone starting after 1 August 2026 makes it unaffordable without external funding.
